The tournament half closes completely; the TOKEN half does not, and the finding concedes as much itself (stat 20112 has no name in itemdata.xml or the v0.682 string table, and duel-token / Golden-Token costs are untouched). Strike the tournament clause only.

Reading further than the finding did confirms it really is a rubber-band: _loc9_ = 10 + (enemyLevel - playerLevel) is a hits-to-kill target that sets elite HP, and _loc10_ = 18 - delta divides player HP to set elite damage. But the OVERTURN fails twice. (2) This code is gated on `if(this.§1t4528s0§)`, the elite flag, and is keyed to the PLAYER's level; it is a different mechanism from the roster-wide level→stat formula the sentence names, which lives in npcdata.xml as data, not as a formula.

new_findings.text: The Focus/crit gating rule closes, but on WEB constants that differ from android on three of five terms, and the per-tick recharge is +1, not +6, in BOTH builds. WEB v0.717: maxreload = 8*24 = 192 frames (§1t99s0§.as:249) against android's 5*24 = 120 (MCSPlayer.as:239). Recharge +1 per tick while reload < maxreload (web §1t99s0§.as:1203-1205; android MCSPlayer.as:1158-1160); the +6 is bonusReload(), whose only caller is NPCManager.as:1711 inside `if(deathCount > 0)` — a KILL bonus (web twin §1t99s0§.as:3320-3323). In-battle stance switch costs a FLAT -48 in web (§1t99s0§.as:3162, inside §1t3489s0§ under the isBattle guard) where android collapses reload>max/2 to max/3 else -max/6 (MCSPlayer.as:3098-3104, inside setStance which opens at :3019). The stance gate is reload >= 48 in web (§1t99s0§.as:3050, :3060) vs reload < maxreload/6 = 20 in android (MCSPlayer.as:2977). Identical in both: zero-at-full on a slash, and the x0.5 / x1 / x1.5 per-stance drain. Nothing about this system needs measuring — but the android numbers are the wrong build's.

new_findings.text: The stance counter-triangle runs in the DEFENDER's frame and the web build has a losing side android lacks. Both x1.2 branches sit inside gotHit (android MCSPlayer.as:3580; web §1t99s0§ — _loc11_ is assigned param2.stance at :3754, param2 being the Damage object), so `this.stance` is the defender and the attacker's stance is the operand. The shipped rule is: Balanced beats Light, Heavy beats Balanced, Light beats Heavy — confirmed independently by the game's own copy, strings.json["6001"]/["6003"]/["6005"]. The WEB build additionally applies x0.9 on each reversed matchup (§1t99s0§.as:3796-3798), which android has no counterpart for: six ordered outcomes, not three. Both terms land BEFORE the DEF subtraction and the min-damage floor.

new_findings.text: The SPEED-stat → skill-cooldown transfer function exists in the WEB build too, and its saturation point is 600, not the android build's 300: cooldownModifier = 1 - min(speed, 600) / 600 * 0.5. It is reached from §1t1523s0§.as:2279-2286 (STAT_SPEED = §1t9410s0§ = 8, x1.5 while the speed buff is up) and consumed at §1t105s0§.as:318, where a skill's cooldown is levelList[level].cooldown * 24 multiplied by the modifier. Porting the android constant halves the benefit at any given SPD (e.g. at SPD 300 android is already at the 0.5 floor while web is at 0.75).

new_findings.text: The SFX side of the audio blocker is closed on both halves, with a precise residual. The DECRYPT is not a whole-file XOR — ResourceManager.decryptByteArray touches only bytes 3..255, swapping ba[i] with ba[i+256] when i%11==0 and then XORing with charCodeAt(1) of the resource name, which is why the raw blob already reads 'CWS' and a naive XOR fails. For Mobile_SoundResource the key is 'o' = 111; the result is a valid CWS v17 SWF (filelen 29,631, inflate 29,623) carrying 13 DefineSound tags and a SymbolClass table naming every one: punch, fart, hitmetal, goodkoto, slash1, slash2, die1, refund, die3, slash3, sumo, die2, deflect. Separately, the WEB payload's own source names 43 distinct "Snd_*" cues at live call sites. So the residual is exact: 13 waveforms recovered, 43 cue names known, 30 cues with no PCM in blob 122.

new_findings.text: The 800x480 native resolution has a WEB-side cite, so it no longer rests on an android file: §1t1540s0§.as:271-273 declares baseW 800, baseH 480 and an ALTERNATE height of 690, and :277-289 selects the 690 layout whenever the viewport is narrower than 800/690. The fit at :294-307 is a single UNIFORM scale with centring — scale = stageWidth/800 with letterbox when the viewport is narrower than 5:3, scale = stageHeight/480 with pillarbox when wider — and :388 hides the four blocker bars when the stage is exactly 800x480 or 800x690. Consequence for film measurement: the shipped renderer never stretches, so the horizontal and vertical scales in a longplay frame are equal by construction, and the 1816-vs-1800 px gap in video A is a recording/re-encode artifact, not a game-side anisotropy.
new_findings.ledger_text: 12. **Native resolution is 800×480 (5:3)**, not 16:9 — HUD x-fractions measured off 1920×1080 video may be pillarbox-compressed. Verify before trusting horizontal coords.
new_findings.lane_impact: UI-HUD ① ('aspect-ratio truth — read stage.stageWidth in a build') closes from source with no build needed; ledger item 12 is CONFIRMED, not overturned, and gains a second supported layout (800x690) it never mentions.

new_findings.text: Every DEF subtraction in both builds is immediately floored by the ATTACKER's minimum damage, so defence can never reduce a hit below that floor — a term the 'DEF is flat subtraction' statement omits. All three web damage paths do `_loc5_ -= getDefense();` then `if(_loc5_ < param2.getMinDamage()) { _loc5_ = param2.getMinDamage(); }`, and android does the same at MCSPlayer.as:3709-3713. A Sim that subtracts DEF without the floor will produce zero-damage hits the original never produces.
new_findings.quote: web §1t99s0§.as:3800 `_loc5_ -= this.§1t4477s0§();` :3801 `if(_loc5_ < param2.§1t1088s0§())` :3803 `_loc5_ = param2.§1t1088s0§();` ‖ android MCSPlayer.as:3709 `damage -= this.getDefense();` :3710 `if(damage < damageObj.getMinDamage())` :3712 `damage = damageObj.getMinDamage();`
